Now they're powering through Sear, carrying as much speed as possible onto the Bentley Straight.

Into the braking zone for Brundle, named after my good friend and fellow commentator.

strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a major factor on this 3.218km layout. Managing the rubber through the long corners will be key.
The pit window here is relatively short, so a well-timed stop can make all the difference.
Fuel consumption will be a concern, especially for those running aggressively early on.
An undercut could be very powerful at Snetterton, with drivers able to gain significant track position in clear air.
The long Bentley Straight provides a good overtaking opportunity, so expect to see some strategic moves there.
With nine turns packed into just over 3 kilometers, the drivers will be working hard to find the optimal balance between speed and tire conservation.
Track position is crucial here. Overtaking can be difficult, so qualifying well is essential.
Late safety cars can really shake things up, providing an opportunity for a cheap pit stop and a chance to gain valuable places.
weatherCommentary: The wind can often play a significant role here at Snetterton, particularly on the exposed sections of the track.
Rain showers can develop quickly in this part of Norfolk, so teams need to be prepared for changeable conditions.
The temperature can fluctuate dramatically throughout the day, affecting tire performance and strategy.
The clear Norfolk skies mean we often see strong sunshine here, which can lead to increased track temperatures.
If the wind picks up, it'll be crucial for the drivers to adjust their lines through the faster corners like Coram.
